statement: You are given a binary tree of non-negative values. The tree is given as the array tree in level order, indexed from 0: the root is tree[0], and the left and right children of the node at index i are at indices 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. null marks a position with no node, and every position below a null must be null too.

Change the values so that the tree satisfies the children sum property: every node that has at least one child holds exactly the sum of its children's values, where a missing child counts as 0. You may only increase values, never decrease them, and you may not change the shape.

Many trees can satisfy this, so here is the method whose result is returned. Going down, if a node's children add up to at least the node's value, set the node to that sum; otherwise raise each existing child to the node's value. Fix both subtrees the same way, then, on the way back up, set the node to the sum of its children.
Return the resulting tree, in the same level-order format as the input.

examples.explanation: 7 + 2 is less than 20, so both children are raised to 20. Below the left 20, 3 and 5 are raised to 20, so that node becomes 40. Below the right 20, 1 + 30 = 31 is already enough. The root ends as 40 + 31 = 71.
4 is raised to 10, then its children 2 and 3 are raised to 10 each, so 4's node becomes 20, and the root, whose only child is now 20, becomes 20 too.
